definitions.explanation: The outermost part or boundary of something.

examples.japanese: テーブルの{端|はし}に{座|すわ}ってください。
examples.english: Please sit at the end of the table.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}の{端|はし}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}いてください。
examples.english: Please write your name at the edge of the paper.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}の{端|はし}を{歩|ある}いてください。
examples.english: Please walk on the edge of the road.

notes:
{端|はし} refers to the outermost edge or end of something.

HOMOPHONES (same pronunciation, different words):
- {端|はし}: edge, end (this word)
- {橋|はし}: bridge
- {箸|はし}: chopsticks
These are distinguished by kanji and pitch accent in speech.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- [noun]の{端|はし}: the edge/end of ~
- {端|はし}から{端|はし}まで: from one end to the other
- {端|はし}に{寄|よ}る: to move to the side/edge

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- テーブルの{端|はし}: edge of the table
- {道|みち}の{端|はし}: side of the road
- {紙|かみ}の{端|はし}: edge of the paper
- ベッドの{端|はし}: edge of the bed

RELATED:
- {端っこ|はしっこ}: corner, edge (casual)
